behavior: A month without a supplied housing event contributes zero event effect.
whyNecessary: The standalone rule accepts only supplied events and needs a neutral result when none is present.
replaceWith: A sourced, recorded housing-event effect for every macro month.

behavior: The layoff rule permits a one-dollar annual pay-coverage tolerance.
whyNecessary: The legacy comparison includes this tolerance and golden equivalence retains it.
replaceWith: A sourced accounting or payroll tolerance for the modeled books.

behavior: Missing town-average pay contributes zero to the hiring threshold.
whyNecessary: The legacy helper defaults to zero when its caller has no town-pay record.
replaceWith: A recorded town-average pay amount or a tagged estimate for the relevant place.

behavior: Persisted macro values retain six decimal places.
whyNecessary: The port preserves legacy replay precision until a persisted-data precision contract is set.
replaceWith: A documented precision contract for macro values.

whyNecessary: The legacy purchase calculation rounds this way for replay equivalence.
replaceWith: A sourced purchase-pricing and currency-rounding policy.

behavior: New hires start at the 25th wage percentile and reach the 75th after 20 years.
whyNecessary: The legacy rule has no sourced tenure curve and these values preserve current behavior.
replaceWith: A measured tenure-to-wage progression by occupation and place.

behavior: The lifted job-rate rule accepts caller-supplied federal/state floor data; local floors are not represented.
whyNecessary: The current source reader supplies no local minimum-wage data.
replaceWith: Place and effective-date keyed local minimum-wage facts.

behavior: Policy-rate midpoint stands in for a 30-year mortgage-rate change.
whyNecessary: The available macro records do not contain a consistent mortgage-rate series for every modeled place and month.
replaceWith: A supplied monthly mortgage-rate series for each place.

behavior: Home-price growth has no housing-supply response term.
whyNecessary: A place-level housing-supply elasticity is not present in the supplied facts.
replaceWith: A sourced supply-elasticity fact and its measured pass-through coefficient.

behavior: The first recorded home-price index starts at 1.
whyNecessary: The pure rule receives a finite macro series and needs a deterministic initial index.
replaceWith: A supplied, source-backed opening index level and date.

behavior: Eviction disposition uses a four-month counsel threshold and a two-month threshold for a lenient judge.
whyNecessary: The legacy disposition rule has no jurisdiction-specific outcome records; both are estimates retained for golden equivalence.
replaceWith: A sourced jurisdiction-specific case-outcome model with counsel and judge facts.

behavior: Home-purchase financing uses a 360-month fixed term.
whyNecessary: The legacy purchase rule uses this term and has no buyer-selected term fact.
replaceWith: A recorded loan term or sourced term distribution for the buyer and loan type.

behavior: Banks do not extend new credit when national credit tightness is 0.75 or higher.
whyNecessary: The legacy bank rule pauses new lines and growth after a national tightening threshold.
replaceWith: A sourced lender-wide credit availability measure and place-level applicability rule.

behavior: A business borrows from the open town bank with the largest deposits; deposit ties use bank ID order.
whyNecessary: Individual business-bank relationships are not supplied to the selection rule.
replaceWith: A recorded business-to-bank relationship and its active loan terms.

behavior: A household head aged 60 or older selects owned outright tenure for a newly chosen home.
whyNecessary: The legacy home selector uses age as a proxy and receives no recorded mortgage balance or paid-off status.
replaceWith: The household's recorded loan balance and home equity at the move date.

behavior: Households of up to two select an apartment fallback; households of five or more may select a large house.
whyNecessary: The legacy home selector uses fixed household-size bands without a sourced household-space model.
replaceWith: A household-space model fitted to recorded resident, room and dwelling facts.
